name: Deterministic rules
summary: Encode the logic as configuration, decision tables, or code. Check native ERP capability first.

whyNot.text: The logic is already known. An LLM would re-derive it probabilistically, add cost and latency, and make the result harder to audit.
Learning a rule you can already state adds training, drift monitoring, and error for no gain.

metrics: Rule coverage (share of items decided without manual touch)
Defect rate found in sample audit
eval.gate: Zero known rule conflicts; exception queue sized for the team that works it

name: Deterministic + fuzzy matching
summary: Exact keys first, then similarity scoring on names, amounts, dates, and references. Route low-confidence matches to a person.

whyNot.text: Matching is a scoring problem over structured fields. String similarity and amount/date tolerances are faster, cheaper, and reproducible. An LLM can help only with reading an unusual free-text reference.
Exact-key rules alone leave the long tail (typos, partial payments, truncated references) to manual work.

metrics: Match precision on a labeled sample (target near 100%)
eval.gate: Precision on auto-matched items meets finance tolerance (typically 99%+) before auto-posting

name: Tabular machine learning
summary: Supervised model (gradient-boosted trees) trained on your historical outcomes, with reason codes per prediction.

whyNot.text: LLMs are not trained on your outcome history and do not produce calibrated probabilities on tabular data. A gradient-boosted model is cheaper per prediction, faster, and gives per-record reason codes.
The signal is a combination of many factors (history, seasonality, counterparty). Hand-written thresholds miss those interactions.

metrics: Lift over current rule or heuristic
eval.baseline: Current rule, heuristic, or 'last value' baseline
eval.gate: Out-of-time backtest beats baseline on the business metric, not only on AUC

name: Anomaly detection + rules
summary: Unsupervised scoring of unusual records, layered on explicit checks. Output is a review queue, not an automatic block.

whyNot.text: Unusualness is a statistical property of your data distribution. An LLM has no view of that distribution.
Without confirmed past cases there is nothing to train a classifier on. Start unsupervised and collect reviewer verdicts as labels.

metrics: Precision of flagged items after review
eval.gate: Flag volume fits reviewer capacity with precision high enough that reviewers keep using it

name: Time-series forecasting
summary: Statistical and ML forecasters benchmarked against a naive baseline, with forecast intervals.

whyNot.text: General LLMs are not forecasting models. Purpose-built statistical, ML, or time-series foundation models are cheaper and measurably better.
Fixed rules such as 'last year plus 5%' ignore trend shifts and seasonality.

eval.gate: Beats seasonal naive on held-out periods for the segments that matter

name: Mathematical optimization
summary: Model the objective and constraints explicitly and solve with an LP/MIP or constraint solver. Planners approve the proposed plan.

whyNot.text: Choosing the best plan under hard constraints is a solver problem. LLMs cannot guarantee feasibility or optimality and will violate constraints silently.
Greedy rules work for simple cases but leave cost on the table when constraints interact.

metrics: Cost or service vs current plan
eval.baseline: Current planner decisions on the same historical scenarios
eval.gate: Zero hard-constraint violations on replayed history and a measurable cost or service gain

name: Document AI + validation rules
summary: Pretrained document models extract fields; rules validate them against master data. Low-confidence fields go to a person.

whyNot.text: For known document types at volume, pretrained document models give per-field confidence, lower cost, and stable output. Use an LLM or vision model as a fallback for the layouts they miss.
Template OCR breaks every time a supplier changes layout.

eval.baseline: Current manual keying time and error rate
eval.gate: Field accuracy on critical fields (amounts, tax, bank) meets finance tolerance with confidence routing on

name: LLM / vision-model extraction
summary: A vision-capable LLM returns fields in a fixed schema. Rules validate the output before anything is posted.

whyNot.text: Layouts vary too much, or the source is free-text email, for pretrained document models to cover well.
Volume and variety make manual keying the bottleneck.

metrics: Field-level accuracy against a labeled set
Hallucinated-field rate (values not present in source)
eval.gate: No hallucinated values on critical fields in the test set; validation rules catch the rest

name: Small / fine-tuned text classifier
summary: Embeddings or a small fine-tuned encoder trained on your labeled text. Cheap at volume and consistent.

whyNot.text: With labeled examples, a small classifier matches or beats a large LLM on a fixed label set at a fraction of the cost and latency.
Keyword rules break on phrasing variation and need constant upkeep.

eval.baseline: Current manual coding or keyword rules
eval.gate: Meets accuracy target on held-out data, with low-confidence items routed to review

name: LLM classification (bootstrap)
summary: A small, fast LLM classifies with few-shot examples while labels are scarce. Plan to replace it with a small classifier once reviewed labels exist.

whyNot.text: There are not yet enough labeled examples to train one. Use the LLM's reviewed outputs to build that label set.
Free text varies too much for keywords to route reliably.

eval.gate: Reviewer agreement meets target; misroutes are recoverable

name: Retrieval-augmented generation
summary: Retrieve the relevant passages the user is allowed to see, then answer with citations. Say 'not covered' when the sources do not answer.

whyNot.text: Policies and contracts are private and change. Without retrieval the model guesses.
Fine-tuning does not reliably teach facts and must be redone whenever documents change.
Keyword search returns documents, not answers. Keep it as the retrieval layer.

metrics: Answer correctness on a question set written by policy owners
eval.baseline: Time to answer by asking the policy owner
eval.gate: No uncited claims on the test set; permission-aware retrieval verified

name: LLM drafting with human review
summary: An LLM drafts text from facts the system already computed. A person reviews before it is sent or filed.

whyNot.text: Fixed templates cannot adapt to account context. Keep templates for legally required wording.
The LLM drafts. It should not decide the facts it is writing about; those come from rules or models upstream.

eval.gate: No factual contradictions with source data in the review sample

name: Tool-using LLM, read-only
summary: An LLM plans lookups across systems through scoped read-only tools and assembles the answer or case file. No writes.

whyNot.text: The lookups needed differ case by case, so a fixed sequence would miss or over-fetch.
Gathering information does not need write access. Keeping it read-only removes most of the risk.

metrics: Task success on a scenario set
eval.baseline: Time for a person to gather the same information
eval.gate: Scenario success meets target; no tool outside the read-only scope is callable

name: Bounded agent with approval gates
summary: An LLM executes multi-step changes through scoped tools. Each write passes an approval gate and value limit.

whyNot.text: Use a fixed workflow if the steps are known. An agent is justified only when the path varies case by case.
Unapproved writes to a system of record are hard to audit and reverse.

metrics: Unauthorized or out-of-policy actions (must be zero)
eval.gate: Zero out-of-policy actions in adversarial and replayed scenarios

name: Human decision, AI prepares
summary: Keep the decision with a person. Automate data gathering around it and record decisions so they can become training data later.

whyNot.text: The logic is not explicit and the cost of a wrong call is high, or there is no history to learn from. Automating now would be guessing.

metrics: Share of decisions recorded with reason codes
eval.gate: Enough recorded decisions to revisit automation
